The Marianas remain on the northern periphery of an unsettled, 
disorganized pattern. Isolated to patchy scattered showers continue 
to propagate west-northwest through the coastal waters, associated 
with increased convergence, troughing, and moisture along the
northern edge of a broad, weak disturbance over Yap State. Himawari
visible satellite imagery shows a very broad, weak cyclonic turning
centered at around 9N142E, to the southeast of Ulithi and Fais in Yap
State. Models show this weak circulation meandering west-northwest
toward Yap Proper over the next day or so, stalling nearby into the
latter half of the week. This will maintain a slightly wetter pattern
for the Marianas over the next day or two with periods of low-end
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms expected through at 
least Tuesday night. The pattern remains messy and certainty is low 
with regards to exact coverage and timing of showers, but a drier
pattern is expected to return for the latter half of the week as the
disturbance near Yap moves away.

Marine/Surf...
Moderate to fresh trade winds will decrease to gentle to moderate
tonight as the regional pressure gradient slackens, then continue to
diminish through the next few days, becoming light to moderate by 
Wednesday. Combined seas of 5 to 8 feet will relax by several feet 
through the next few days as the trade swell diminishes, becoming 3 
to 5 feet by Wednesday. Trade winds and swell will come back up this
weekend, becoming 5 to 7 feet once more on Saturday. Due to the
diminishing trade swell, surf has decreased along east facing reefs
and the high risk of rip currents along east reefs was allowed to
expire this afternoon. A moderate risk of rip currents along north, 
east, and south facing reefs will continue, decreasing to low risk
for south reefs over the next day or so. There will be a moderate 
risk for lightning tonight through Tuesday night. A high risk of rip 
currents may return along east facing reefs late this coming weekend 
as the trade wind and swell reinvigorate.

Eastern Micronesia...
Latest satellite imagery shows partly cloudy skies with spotty 
showers over Pohnpei and Kosrae, with mostly cloudy skies and 
scattered showers over Majuro. Altimetry shows seas of 4 to 7 feet 
across the region.

Conditions are fairly quiet across eastern Micronesia this 
afternoon, with only low-end scattered showers across Majuro, and 
isolated showers elsewhere. Latest model guidance shows that this 
should change over the coming days. A weak Inter-Tropical Convergence
Zone (ITCZ) is seen across the Marshalls, generating scattered to 
numerous showers from the Date Line to Kwajalein, north of Majuro. 
The ITCZ looks to strengthen over the coming days as it stretches 
west across eastern Micronesia. This feature is expected to interact 
with passing weak trade-wind troughs to produce periods of scattered 
to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms across the region 
through at least the middle of the week. Kosrae and Majuro look to 
see the longest period of numerous showers, with Pohnpei expected to 
dry a little by Wednesday. Models are showing the ITCZ remaining 
active into the weekend, however, they tend to keep the ITCZ active a
bit longer than it actually does. Therefore, decreased coverage for 
showers to around 40 to 50 percent beginning Thursday and continuing 
into the weekend.

For the marine forecast, conditions look to remain fairly benign for
the next few days, with seas remaining between 4 and 6 feet for
Kosrae and Pohnpei and between 5 and 7 feet for Majuro. Seas look to
build slightly near the end of the week and into the weekend, but
will remain below the 10 foot threshold for a Small Craft Advisory.
Winds look to remain mostly light to gentle for Pohnpei and Kosrae,
with occasional moderate winds at Pohnpei through Tuesday. For
Majuro, gentle to moderate winds are expected into the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
There are two main features that will bring unsettling weather to 
the region. The first is a broad surface trough with a weak embedded
circulation though central Yap State, and the second is a trade-wind
trough east of Chuuk lagoon.

The broad trough with a weak embedded circulation will bring 
scattered showers to Yap Proper tonight through Wednesday. Showers 
produced by this trough are expected to bring up to 2 inches of rain 
through Wednesday. Then, Yap Proper will have a short reprieve until 
the trough near Chuuk moves through the area near the weekend. 
Overall, a wet week is in store for Yap.

For Palau, the dry spell is expected to continue through this week,
however the trough near Chuuk may bring showers to the region for
this weekend.

For Chuuk, the trade-wind trough is expected to start moving through
the region this evening bringing numerous locally heavy showers and
isolated thunderstorms to the lagoon and surrounding islands. These
showers are expected to begin tapering down during the day Tuesday.
